references.title: Stream composer: "Announce to class" box with All students picker
references.question: Q1
references.take: The class Stream page pairs a lightweight "Announce something to your class" text box with a "For / All students" audience dropdown directly above it, showing that audience targeting can live as one control next to the compose field instead of a separate step.

references.title: Dub link analytics: clicks/leads/sales for a tagged share link
references.question: Q4
references.take: Dub's Analytics view shows Clicks/Leads/Sales counters plus a time-series chart for links filtered by tag, evidence that link-level delivery feedback can be a few aggregate counters and a trend line rather than a per-recipient log of who clicked.

references.title: Spotify notification settings: per-category Email/Push toggles
references.question: Q6
references.take: Spotify's Notification settings list content categories (Music, Podcasts, Audiobooks, Concerts, Livestreams), each with its own Email and Push checkboxes, modeling how a learner-facing portal could let people set per-category channel preferences for course communications.

references.title: The Leap: broadcast composer with template, editor, and recipient segments
references.question: Q1
references.take: The Leap's broadcast flow chains a template chooser into a rich-text editor with a dedicated recipients dropdown for picking one or more contact segments, then forces a review-and-confirm modal before send and finishes on a sent-state screen with immediate analytics — a model for pairing audience targeting with an explicit confirm step in a course composer.

references.title: Teachable: compose and send a broadcast email to a recipient group
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable's Compose flow (built to compose "a new announcement or message to users") has the course admin write a subject/body, pick a recipient group, confirm in a modal, and land on a success acknowledgement — showing that a minimal 4-screen composer-plus-confirm pattern is enough for an announcement tool inside an education product.

references.title: LinkedIn: compose a post, then open a date/time scheduling dialog
references.question: Q1
references.take: LinkedIn's composer exposes a scheduling entry point in the compose toolbar that opens a dedicated date-and-time picker before the post is queued, showing how scheduling can be an optional side-dialog off the main composer rather than a separate screen or mode.

references.title: Loom: share dialog with per-person permission level and invited list
references.question: Q3
references.take: Loom's Share dialog lets the owner add a person or Space and set a permission level (e.g. Can view) before sending the invite, then confirms the person now appears in an invited/access list — a pattern for showing who currently has access to a shared item, not just generating a link.

references.title: Dropbox: generate a folder view-only link, then review its link settings
references.question: Q3
references.take: Dropbox's Create Folder View Link flow separates link generation from link management: after the viewing link is created, a Link Settings screen surfaces the access controls for that specific link — a clean split between "create the link" and "configure/audit the link" that a course materials share dialog could mirror.
